verdict.rationale: Granola's docs say it automatically generates AI-enhanced notes once a call ends, with templates that shape the summary format, source tracing back to the transcript, and a shareable link, which covers the core of a post-meeting summary you can share. The docs never say these notes are organised into key points, decisions and next steps, and nothing shows they are good enough to share without editing; one PM said Granola action items 'tended to slip through', though it is unclear whether that means poor extraction or poor follow-up. missing for 10: documented key-points/decisions/next-steps structure, evidence that summaries are share-ready without editing, independent hands-on corroboration of action-item quality

support.subject: As a product manager, I get a structured summary right after each meeting — key points, decisions, and next steps — good enough to share without editing

citations.quote: Once Granola has recognised your call has ended, or you stop it manually, it will automatically generate enhanced notes.
While Granola's default summarisation adapts to a range of formats, you might want to choose a specific template (or set up your own!) for a specific type of call
Copy link will copy a unique URL link to the meeting notes, which you can send to others.
Use the magnifying glass beside each note to see where in the transcript or raw notes the note came from
